sentences.text: This witness is found to have asserted that the accused had demanded money for purchase of tempo  10 S.C.No.1371/2014 traveler.
This may be inconsistent with the version in the first information statement of C.W.1.
It may also be a fact that C.W.1 had not deposed regarding this aspect in his testimony.
Merely on account of this variation it cannot be held that the prosecution story is unbelievable.
The witness had also deposed regarding the cruelty meted out to the deceased by the accused.
During the cross examination it was elicited through this witness that the engagement was organised in the house of Sri Honnagiriyappa a relative to both these witnesses and the accused.
11. The witness had denied the suggestion that prior to the engagement the first accused used to frequently visit the house of this witness.
Therefore it is clear that neither the family members of this witness nor the accused had occasions to frequently visit each others' houses.
Under such circumstances it was not  11 S.C.No.1371/2014 possible to know the mindset of the members of the family of the accused.
Even if there were frequent visits one cannot judge the intent of another person with all acquaintances.

Therefore it is not a rule that merely because there was sufficient opportunity to K.R.Puram P.S vs Rajesh S on 6 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109716825/
7 gather information regarding the attitude of the members of the family of the accused the family members of this witness had gathered information regarding the family background of the accused.
It is also not a rule that merely because initially the accused had not placed demands for dowry that this would remain an eternal truth in future as well.
12. This witness had denied the suggestion that the deceased had decided to end her life on account of ill health.

If this was the case the accused ought to have placed materials as to the ailments the deceased was suffering, whether the accused had taken her to  12 S.C.No.1371/2014 the hospital, or at least an attempt was made to inform this witness and her family members regarding the ill health if this witness had no knowledge.
There is no suggestion found to be made to this witness regarding her knowledge of ailments suffered by the deceased.
There is absolutely no materials to show that the deceased was suffering from ailments that could have prompted her to end her life.
If at all the deceased was suffering from such ailments it would this witness who would have been informed.
13. In the absence of any materials regarding the ailments suffered by the deceased the defence of ailment as the cause for suicide does not hold water.
